title: Setting Up Raspberry Pi
subtitle: OS installation, SSH, and initial configuration

content.text: Raspberry Pi runs a full Linux OS (Raspberry Pi OS). Flash the SD card with Raspberry Pi Imager, enable SSH, and connect headlessly.

content.code:
# Flash with Raspberry Pi Imager (GUI) or
# via command line
sudo dd if=raspios.img of=/dev/sdX bs=4M status=progress

# Enable SSH before first boot
touch /boot/ssh

# Set WiFi credentials
cat > /boot/wpa_supplicant.conf << EOF
country=IN
ctrl_interface=DIR=/var/run/wpa_supplicant GROUP=netdev
update_config=1
network={
  ssid="YourNetwork"
  psk="YourPassword"
}
EOF

# Connect
ssh pi@raspberrypi.local

content.text: Use Raspberry Pi Imager's advanced settings to preconfigure hostname, SSH, and WiFi — no manual file editing needed.

questions.question: How do you enable SSH headlessly on Raspberry Pi?
options: Place an empty file named "ssh" in the /boot partition
questions.explanation: Placing an empty file named "ssh" in the /boot partition tells the Pi to enable SSH on first boot.

faq.q: What operating system does Raspberry Pi use?
faq.a: Raspberry Pi OS (formerly Raspbian), based on Debian Linux. You can also run Ubuntu, Arch, or other ARM-compatible Linux distributions.
